title: Reel: why your fork feels harsh on small stuff
caption:
Harsh on the small stuff usually isn't the spring. Every little bump has to push oil through the piston, and if compression is set too firm the fork just skips across the top.

Back it off a click at a time and the fork starts moving with the ground instead of fighting it.

Tell Dialed Offroad it felt harsh on small bumps and it tells you which clicker and which way. Link in bio.

Where does your bike feel harshest, the chop or the big hits?

title: Reel: the shock's low-speed clicker
caption:
Most shocks have two compression adjusters on the reservoir. The small clicker is low-speed: it controls the slow stuff, like how much the rear squats when you get on the gas.

One click in and the rear holds up more. One click out and it sits down and hooks up. The big nut is high-speed, set in turns, and that's for the hard hits.

Dialed Offroad tells you which one to move and which way, counted out from fully closed. Link in bio.

Does your rear squat on corner exits or feel too stiff to hook up?
tt_title: What the low-speed shock clicker does
note: Animated explainer (oneclick: oneclick-shock-lsc), made by Claude

title: Reel: rebound, too fast vs too slow
caption:
Rebound is the half of the clicker story most riders skip. After every hit the oil flows back through the piston, and the rebound clicker sets how fast the fork returns.

Too fast and the front gets light and deflects. Too slow and it can't come back between bumps, so it packs down and turns harsh.

Tell Dialed Offroad how the front felt and it tells you which way to go, one click at a time. Link in bio.
